title: B1 review: a real conversation
why: This big review brings together all of level B1 (opinion and the subjunctive, hypotheses, the past conditional, storytelling tenses, relative pronouns, por / para, reported speech) around a long conversation about work, life plans and a trip to Latin America. It closes level B1 and checks that the learner is ready for level B2.

{"lessons": ["

Your B1 toolbox

You've reached the end of level B1. Here, at a glance, is everything that now lets you hold a real conversation. Each row matches a lesson in the level: if a structure feels fuzzy, go back and review it.

To…StructureExample
give your opinioncreo que + indicative / no creo que + subjunctiveCreo que tienes razón. / No creo que sea fácil.
express a wishquiero que, espero que, ojalá + subjunctiveEspero que te guste.
talk about the future after cuandocuando + subjunctiveCuando llegues, llámame.
imaginesi + imperfect subjunctive + conditionalSi pudiera, viviría en Granada.
express regrethabría + participleHabría preferido ir en tren.
link the past to the presentpretérito perfectoHoy he madrugado mucho.
tell a storyimperfecto, indefinido, pluscuamperfectoLlovía y me di cuenta de que había olvidado el paraguas.
be specificque, quien, donde, lo queEs el pueblo donde nació mi abuela.
generalizeimpersonal seEn España se cena tarde.
express purpose, causepara / porEs para ti. / Gracias por todo.
report speechdijo que + tenses shifting backMe dijo que vendría.

In a conversation, nobody expects perfection: people expect you to get your meaning across and keep the exchange going. But these structures make the difference between “survival” Spanish and a real B1.

", "

Traps for English speakers

Here are the most common mistakes English speakers make at level B1. Reread your messages with this list in mind.

AvoidSayWhy
Si tendría tiempo…Si tuviera tiempo…Never the conditional after si (just like “if I would”).
Cuando llegas mañana…Cuando llegues mañana…Cuando + a future event = present subjunctive, even though English uses the plain present.
Quiero tú venir.Quiero que vengas.“I want you to…” = querer que + subjunctive.
Me dijo venir.Me dijo que viniera.A reported command = que + subjunctive.
Espero que estás bien.Espero que estés bien.Esperar que always takes the subjunctive.
Estudio por aprobar.Estudio para aprobar.Purpose (“in order to”) = para + infinitive.
El libro leo es bueno.El libro que leo es bueno.The relative que can never be dropped.
Según a el estudio…Según el estudio…Según takes no preposition, unlike “according to.”
La gente son simpáticos.La gente es simpática.La gente is feminine singular, unlike “people are.”
Conozco Marta.Conozco a Marta.A person as direct object takes the personal a.

A reflex to keep

Before conjugating, ask yourself two questions: which time (present, past linked to the present, finished past, past of the past, future) and which mood (a fact = indicative; a wish, a doubt, a future after cuando = subjunctive; a hypothesis = conditional). These two questions settle most hesitations.

", "

Keeping a conversation going

Speaking isn't just making correct sentences: it's also keeping things going, reacting and buying time. These little words bring your Spanish to life.

To…Spanish
buy timePues… / A ver… / Bueno… / ¿Cómo te diría?
keep it going¿Y tú qué opinas? / ¿Y qué pasó después? / ¿En serio?
react¡Qué envidia! / ¡No me digas! / ¡Qué fuerte! / ¡Qué bien!
add nuanceDepende. / Por un lado…, por otro… / No estoy del todo de acuerdo.
rephraseO sea… / Es decir… / Lo que quiero decir es que…

In Spain, after a meal with family or friends, people stay at the table chatting for hours: it's the sobremesa. It's the perfect moment to practice everything you've learned.

Next stop: Latin America

If you travel to Peru, Colombia or Mexico, your Spanish from Spain will be understood everywhere. A few differences worth knowing so you can understand the people you talk to:

In SpainIn Latin AmericaEnglish
vosotros tenéisustedes tienenyou (all) have
el cocheel carro, el autothe car
el móvilel celularthe cell phone
el ordenadorla computadorathe computer
conducirmanejarto drive
coger el autobústomar el autobústo take the bus

In several Latin American countries, the verb coger has a vulgar meaning. There, say tomar instead: tomar un taxi, tomar el autobús.
